chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The bird comes from the remote place.' He said: 'But rather, it comes for its sustenance.'

key_terms.الطَّيْر: The bird — used as a proverbial example of a creature traveling to seek food
key_terms.الْمَكَان الْبَعِيد: The remote/distant place — emphasizing the seemingly purposeless journey
key_terms.رِزْق: Divinely ordained sustenance/provision — what God has apportioned for each creature

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about birds traveling from faraway places in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Is'haq ibn Ammar asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about a bird traveling from a distant place, and the Imam redirects the inquiry to highlight divine providence: the bird does not travel aimlessly but is drawn by God-ordained sustenance (rizq). This brief hadith teaches that all creatures, even birds, are guided by divine provision. The concept of rizq (divinely allocated sustenance) was well understood by the Imam's audience as a central tenet of Islamic theology affirming God's role as the ultimate Provider (al-Razzaq).
